questions.question: Which of the following is a non-infectious disease?

solution.key_concept: Infectious diseases pass from one person to another. Non-infectious diseases do not.
steps: Typhoid, malaria and AIDS spread from person to person, so they are infectious.
Cancer does not pass from one person to another, so it is non-infectious.
solution.why_not_others: Typhoid (bacterial), malaria (protozoan) and AIDS (viral) are all infectious diseases.
solution.common_trap: Assuming any major cause of death must be infectious. Cancer is a major non-infectious cause of death.

questions.question: A pathogen that enters the body through contaminated food and settles in the intestine must be adapted to the host environment. Which adaptation is essential for it?
options: Resistance to stomach acid and digestive enzymes
Ability to form gametocytes in RBCs

solution.key_concept: A pathogen must adapt to its environment within the host.
steps: A food-borne pathogen passes through the stomach before it reaches the intestine.
On the way, it meets stomach acid and digestive enzymes.
Intestinal pathogens therefore resist stomach acid and digestive enzymes.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Resistance to stomach acid and digestive enzymes
solution.why_not_others: UV resistance has nothing to do with life inside the gut. Gametocyte formation and haemozoin release are features of Plasmodium in the blood, not of intestinal pathogens.
solution.common_trap: Picking a familiar pathogen feature, such as haemozoin, that has nothing to do with the intestinal environment.

questions.question: Which of the following lists contains only groups of pathogens?

solution.key_concept: Pathogens are disease-causing organisms: bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoans and helminths.
steps: Check each list against the five pathogen groups.
Mosquitoes and houseflies are vectors, mast cells are host cells, and carcinogens are cancer-causing agents.
Only bacteria, fungi, protozoans and helminths are all pathogen groups.
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 includes vectors. Option 2 includes mast cells, which are host immune cells. Option 4 includes carcinogens, which are not organisms.
solution.common_trap: Confusing vectors, which carry pathogens, with the pathogens themselves.

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Health is defined simply as the absence of disease.
statements.R: Health depends on genetic factors, infections, lifestyle and a balanced mind.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease.
steps: A is false: health is more than the absence of disease.
R is true: genetic factors, infections, lifestyle and a balanced mind all affect health.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so options 1, 2 and 3 cannot be correct.
solution.common_trap: Accepting the everyday meaning of health, absence of disease, instead of the full definition.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: To cause disease, a pathogen must enter the body, multiply and interfere with the normal functions of the host.
statements.II: Houseflies act as mechanical carriers of Entamoeba histolytica, which is an example of disease spread through vectors.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Pathogens enter, multiply and disrupt host function. Vectors such as houseflies help spread disease.
steps: Statement I matches the requirements a pathogen must meet to cause disease, so it is correct.
Houseflies are mechanical carriers of Entamoeba histolytica, and houseflies are listed as vectors, so Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are factually correct, so options that reject either one are wrong.
solution.common_trap: Thinking only mosquitoes count as vectors. Houseflies also spread pathogens.

questions.question: Common cold is caused by

solution.key_concept: Common cold is a viral infection of the nose and respiratory passage.
steps: Rhinoviruses infect the nose and respiratory passage but not the lungs.
Common cold lasts 3-7 days.
solution.why_not_others: Plasmodium causes malaria, Salmonella typhi causes typhoid, and Streptococcus pneumoniae causes pneumonia.
solution.common_trap: Confusing common cold with pneumonia, which is bacterial and infects the alveoli.

questions.question: Which event in the life cycle of Plasmodium takes place in the human body?
options: Asexual multiplication in liver cells and RBCs
Storage of sporozoites in salivary glands
Development of the zygote in the gut

solution.key_concept: Humans are the intermediate host of Plasmodium, where it reproduces only asexually.
steps: Sporozoites enter humans through the bite of a female Anopheles mosquito.
They multiply asexually, first in liver cells and then in RBCs.
Fertilisation, development and storage of sporozoites in the salivary glands all occur in the mosquito.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Asexual multiplication in liver cells and RBCs
solution.why_not_others: Fertilisation, zygote development and sporozoite storage in the salivary glands all happen inside the mosquito, which is the definitive host.
solution.common_trap: Thinking Plasmodium reproduces sexually in human RBCs because gametocytes form there.

questions.question: A patient has a sustained high fever of 39-40 degrees C, weakness, stomach pain, constipation, headache and loss of appetite. Which test would confirm the most likely disease?

solution.key_concept: These symptoms are typical of typhoid, which is confirmed by the Widal test.
steps: A sustained 39-40 degrees C fever with constipation, stomach pain and loss of appetite points to typhoid, caused by Salmonella typhi.
Typhoid is confirmed by the Widal test.
solution.why_not_others: Bone marrow tests are used for leukaemia. MRI and histopathological study are used in cancer detection.
solution.common_trap: Picking a general diagnostic method instead of the specific test for typhoid.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Each disease is caused by a specific pathogen.
steps: Filariasis is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti (A-III).
Amoebiasis is caused by Entamoeba histolytica (B-IV).
Ringworm is caused by Trichophyton (C-I).
Pneumonia is caused by Haemophilus influenzae (D-II).
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps the pathogens of amoebiasis and ringworm. Option 2 swaps the pathogens of filariasis and amoebiasis. Option 3 swaps the pathogens of ringworm and pneumonia.
solution.common_trap: Assigning the fungal genus Trichophyton to a protozoan disease, or Entamoeba to a skin infection.
solution.time_saving_tip: Once A-III and B-IV are fixed, only option 3 and option 4 remain; C-I then settles the answer.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about human diseases are correct?

statements.A: Plasmodium falciparum causes the most serious, malignant form of malaria.
statements.B: Rhinoviruses infect the nose and respiratory passage but not the lungs.
statements.C: Dengue and chikungunya are protozoan diseases spread by Anopheles mosquitoes.
statements.D: In pneumonia, the alveoli fill with fluid, and the lips and fingernails may turn grey to bluish.
statements.E: Entamoeba histolytica lives in the small intestine of humans.

solution.key_concept: Recall the pathogen, vector and site of infection for each disease.
steps: A is correct: P. falciparum causes malignant malaria.
B is correct: common cold does not affect the lungs.
C is incorrect: dengue and chikungunya are viral and spread by Aedes.
D is correct: these are signs of pneumonia.
E is incorrect: Entamoeba histolytica lives in the large intestine.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A, B and D only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1, 3 and 4 each include C or E, both of which are false.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the vectors Aedes and Anopheles, or the small and large intestine.

questions.question: Which antibody crosses the placenta from mother to foetus?

solution.key_concept: Placental IgG gives the foetus passive immunity.
steps: IgG crosses the placenta.
IgA is abundant in colostrum, IgE mediates allergy, and IgM is the largest antibody (a pentamer).
solution.why_not_others: IgA reaches the infant through colostrum, not the placenta. IgE is involved in allergy. IgM is too large to cross the placenta.
solution.common_trap: Confusing placental IgG with colostral IgA.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary lymphoid organ?

solution.key_concept: Primary lymphoid organs (bone marrow and thymus) are where lymphocytes form and mature.
steps: Bone marrow and thymus are the primary lymphoid organs.
Spleen, tonsils and Peyer's patches are secondary lymphoid organs.
solution.why_not_others: Spleen, tonsils and Peyer's patches are all secondary lymphoid organs.
solution.common_trap: Calling the large, blood-filtering spleen a primary organ.

questions.question: Which of the following gives a person passive immunity?
options: Hepatitis B vaccine produced in yeast
A booster dose of a vaccine

solution.key_concept: Passive immunity comes from ready-made antibodies. Active immunity comes from the body's own response to antigens.
steps: Antivenom contains preformed antibodies, so it gives quick, passive immunity.
Vaccines (including boosters) and infections make the body produce its own antibodies, which is active immunity.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Antivenom injected after a snakebite
solution.why_not_others: The vaccine, the booster dose and recovery from infection all stimulate the body's own antibody response, so they give active immunity.
solution.common_trap: Assuming that anything injected gives passive immunity. Vaccines give active immunity.

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: A second encounter with the same pathogen produces a stronger and faster immune response than the first encounter.
statements.R: The first encounter with a pathogen generates memory B and T cells.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Acquired immunity has memory, which produces the secondary (anamnestic) response.
steps: A is true: the secondary response is stronger and faster than the low-intensity primary response.
R is true: memory cells form after the first exposure. Vaccines work on the same principle.
These memory cells are the reason the second response is faster and stronger, so R explains A.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true and directly linked, which rules out options 2, 3 and 4.
solution.common_trap: Thinking the primary response is the stronger one.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Cell-mediated immunity, which is responsible for graft rejection, is provided by B-lymphocytes.
statements.II: Allergy is an exaggerated IgG response in which mast cells release histamine and serotonin.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: T-lymphocytes give cell-mediated immunity. IgE mediates allergy.
steps: Statement I is incorrect: cell-mediated immunity comes from T-lymphocytes, while B-lymphocytes give humoral immunity.
Statement II is incorrect: allergy is an exaggerated IgE response, not an IgG response.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Each statement contains one wrong term (B instead of T, and IgG instead of IgE), so neither statement is correct.
solution.common_trap: Accepting statement II because the histamine and serotonin part is correct.

questions.question: Cancer cells divide uncontrollably because they have lost

solution.key_concept: Normal cells stop dividing when they touch other cells, a property called contact inhibition.
steps: Cancer cells lose contact inhibition.
They keep dividing and form tumours.
solution.why_not_others: Cancer cells clearly keep the ability to divide, and they still respire and make proteins.
solution.common_trap: Thinking cancer is a gain of division ability rather than a loss of the control on division.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-ionising radiation that acts as a carcinogen?

solution.key_concept: Carcinogenic radiation can be ionising or non-ionising.
steps: X-rays and gamma rays are ionising carcinogens.
UV radiation is a non-ionising carcinogen.
CT scans use X-rays, which are ionising.
solution.why_not_others: X-rays, gamma rays and the X-rays used in CT scans are all ionising radiations.
solution.common_trap: Forgetting that CT relies on X-rays, which are ionising.

questions.question: Which technique for detecting cancer uses strong magnetic fields and non-ionising radiation?

solution.key_concept: MRI uses strong magnetic fields and non-ionising radiation.
steps: Radiography and CT both use X-rays.
Biopsy is the removal of tissue for histopathological study, not an imaging method.
MRI uses magnetic fields and non-ionising radiation.
solution.why_not_others: Radiography and CT use ionising X-rays. Biopsy is not an imaging technique.
solution.common_trap: Confusing CT (X-rays, 3-D images) with MRI (magnetic fields).

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Biological response modifier that activates the immune system against tumours

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Cellular genes that can be activated to transform cells

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Tissue sample taken for histopathological study

solution.key_concept: Cancer detection methods, treatments and oncogenes each have a distinct role.
steps: Alpha-interferon is a biological response modifier (A-II).
Biopsy is followed by histopathological study (B-IV).
CT uses X-rays to produce 3-D images (C-I).
Proto-oncogenes (c-onc) can be activated to transform cells (D-III).
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps the matches for interferon and biopsy. Option 2 swaps the matches for CT and proto-oncogenes. Option 4 swaps the matches for interferon and proto-oncogenes.
solution.common_trap: Linking interferon to genes instead of to immunotherapy.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about cancer are correct?

statements.A: Benign tumours invade surrounding tissues and metastasise.
statements.B: Leukaemia is detected by blood and bone marrow tests.
statements.D: Chemotherapy can cause side effects such as hair loss and anaemia.
statements.E: MRI uses X-rays to produce images of internal organs.

solution.key_concept: Know the tumour types, detection methods and treatment side effects.
steps: A is incorrect: benign tumours stay localised. Only malignant tumours invade and metastasise.
B is correct: leukaemia is detected by blood and bone marrow tests.
C is correct: oncogenic viruses carry viral oncogenes.
D is correct: chemotherapy can cause hair loss and anaemia.
E is incorrect: MRI uses magnetic fields and non-ionising radiation, while CT uses X-rays.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): B, C and D only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1, 2 and 4 each include A or E, both of which are false.
solution.common_trap: Reversing the properties of benign and malignant tumours, or of MRI and CT.
